data_and_features: Form 4 filings only, no technical or fundamental filters
model_or_rule: Enter on cluster detection, fixed 30/60/90-day hold
main_result: Looked profitable but the universe was hand-picked and tiny
rationale: Selection bias: 16 tickers were chosen by eye, not discovered systematically; not trustworthy evidence either way

model_or_rule: Same cluster-entry rule as EXP-01, run market-wide
main_result: Near-zero Sharpe, max gain +33,580% (a data artifact)
rationale: Unadjusted stock splits corrupted raw prices on several tickers, producing absurd outlier trades; result not usable until a data-quality guard exists

model_or_rule: Same cluster-entry rule, price floor added
main_result: Split-corruption outliers gone, but mean return and Sharpe flat-to-negative on 60/90-day holds
rationale: Fixed the data-quality bug but exposed that the signal itself had no real edge yet; a price floor alone was not the fix

hypothesis_version: v1, with cluster-value floor and entry trailing stop
model_or_rule: Cluster-entry rule + trailing stop from entry
main_result: Noise trades cut 87%, but mean return and Sharpe negative at every holding period; win rate decayed 30->90 day
rationale: Root cause: insiders are contrarian buyers, so trend logic fights the signal; a trailing stop from entry whipsaws on the gap-downs common in this universe

model_or_rule: Cluster-entry rule with routine buys excluded
main_result: First real-data run with all Tier-1/Tier-2 filters active still returned negative Sharpe at every holding period
rationale: Filters are directionally correct per the literature but not sufficient alone; the exit rule (still trailing-stop-only at this point) was the bigger problem

model_or_rule: Cluster-entry rule + short-interest overlap filter
main_result: 2.0 won on both train and test Sharpe; became the standing default
rationale: Insider buying against a crowded short is a stronger contrarian signal than insider buying alone, and 2.0 generalized out of sample

model_or_rule: 4 exit variants at 15%/30%: trail-only, trail+take-profit, fixed-stop+take-profit, fixed-stop-only
main_result: Fixed stop-loss + take-profit (no trailing) was the only variant positive at every holding period
rationale: This became the first configuration with a real, sign-consistent edge; adopted as STOP_LOSS_PCT=0.15, TAKE_PROFIT_PCT=0.30, TRAILING_STOP=False

model_or_rule: Same exit rule, 20 bps round-trip cost added
main_result: Edge shrank substantially but stayed positive at every holding period
rationale: Realistic costs are mandatory for the result to mean anything; 0.002 kept as the standing assumption for every later experiment

model_or_rule: Same exit rule, train/test split by entry date
main_result: Mixed and weak, at or below the noise floor
rationale: Edge was not yet convincingly out-of-sample; treated as unconfirmed pending further refinement

model_or_rule: Same exit rule
main_result: Edge held its sign on both train and test for the first time in the project
rationale: Upgraded the read from leans-toward-noise to a real but weak edge; justified moving on to universe/liquidity filters

data_and_features: Same as EXP-10 + 20-day avg dollar volume
model_or_rule: Same exit rule, liquidity floor added
main_result: Turned every holding period negative (60-day total return +16.8% -> -9.2%)
rationale: The edge concentrates in micro-cap/illiquid names; a liquidity floor removes exactly the trades that work

data_and_features: Same as EXP-10 + 20-day avg dollar volume
model_or_rule: Same exit rule, upper ceiling instead of a floor
main_result: $12M looked good on train (Sharpe 0.064) but negative on test (-0.058); $2.5M held on both; 60-day drawdown -38.3%->-10.5%, return +16.8%->+22.4%, Sharpe ~3x to 1.189
rationale: $12M is an overfit to the training window; $2.5M is the single biggest improvement found in the project and generalizes

model_or_rule: Same exit rule
main_result: Hurt badly again; test Sharpe negative at every holding period
rationale: Confirms the edge concentrates below $5/share even after the volume ceiling; MIN_PRICE stays disabled

data_and_features: cluster size, conviction ratio, days-to-cover, dollar volume, entry price vs. trade_return
model_or_rule: Correlation analysis, no new trading rule
main_result: Every feature came in under 0.02 correlation with trade_return
rationale: No usable basis for feature-based position sizing; dropped the idea rather than force a spurious tilt

model_or_rule: Position size = current equity x position_size_pct
main_result: Beat static sizing on return and Sharpe with no extra drawdown; Sharpe never changes with pure compounding since it scales the whole return stream proportionally
rationale: Confirmed compounding is strictly better than static, but a further improvement (house-money) was found next

model_or_rule: Protected principal at position_size_pct, profit cushion above initial capital at aggressive_pct
main_result: 0.08 gave the best Sharpe at every holding period for almost no extra drawdown
rationale: Genuine improvement in curve shape, not just a rescaling; adopted as the sizing default

data_and_features: Trade return distribution per holding period
model_or_rule: Full-Kelly and half-Kelly position-size calculation
main_result: Full-Kelly 4.4%-5.9%, half-Kelly 2.7%-3.0%, closely matching an independently derived ~2.56% capacity ceiling from max concurrent open positions (39 at 60-day)
rationale: Two unrelated methods agree; POSITION_SIZE_PCT=0.02 kept as capital-realistic rather than arbitrary

model_or_rule: New-trade size / (1 + decay_rate x num_open_positions)
main_result: Even mild decay cut total return by more than half for almost no Sharpe benefit
rationale: This strategy runs near-permanently crowded, not occasionally crowded, so throttling on concurrency mostly just starves good trades

asset_universe: Full market, capital split 1/3 each across 30/60/90-day
model_or_rule: Equal-weight blend of the 30/60/90-day sleeves
main_result: Underperformed the single best sleeve alone on both return and Sharpe
rationale: The weakest sleeve (90-day) drags the blend down; no diversification benefit large enough to offset that

model_or_rule: Fixed stop until trade is up trail_activation_pct, then trail at trail_pct, 30% take-profit stays active as backstop
main_result: 50% activation is a clear peak: 60-day portfolio Sharpe 1.280->2.139, total return +31.8%->+109.4%, for only a small extra drawdown; only 32-46 of ~890 trades per period use the trail
rationale: Confirmed as a genuine local peak via a fine grid around 40%-70%, not a fluke; adopted as TRAIL_ACTIVATION_PCT=0.50, TRAIL_PCT=0.15

model_or_rule: No take-profit cap; two-stage partial exit; ratcheting trail width; ATR-based trail; time-gated activation; liquidity-tiered targets
main_result: Best of the six (ratcheting trail width) reached Sharpe 1.589, still well short of EXP-20's plain activation trail
rationale: More moving parts did not beat the simpler mechanic; kept the simpler rule per the assignment's own preference for simplicity

model_or_rule: Same activation-trail mechanic as EXP-20
key_parameters: trail_activation_pct=0.30 (user choice, in place of the data-optimal 0.50)
main_result: Lower risk, lower reward: 60-day Sharpe 1.276, total return 37.6%, versus 2.139/+109.4% at 50%
rationale: Applied per explicit user preference for lower risk, then reversed once the stop-loss sweep below gave a better risk/reward combination

model_or_rule: Same activation-trail mechanic as EXP-20
main_result: Widening 15%->20% at 30-day/50%-activation lifts total return 103.3%->132.3% for only a small extra drawdown (Sharpe 2.107->2.088); same widening hurts 60-day since the setting is global; 25% pushes return higher but Sharpe/drawdown degrade further
rationale: 20% is the better stopping point for the 30-day primary configuration; reverses EXP-22 back to 50% activation

hypothesis_version: v4, position-size dial check on final combo
model_or_rule: Same exit rule as EXP-23
main_result: Sharpe stays roughly flat across the range while return and drawdown shrink together
rationale: Size is a pure volatility dial here, not a free improvement; kept 2%/8% given the project's risk appetite

model_or_rule: Independent entry-date-ordered, cash-tracking simulator built specifically to validate EXP-23's numbers
key_parameters: n/a (diagnostic, not a new trading rule)
main_result: Disagreed with production: 113.7%/1.986 vs. reported 132.3%/2.088, despite zero trades ever skipped for lack of cash
rationale: Found that simulate_dynamic() sized trades in exit-date order, letting a later-entering trade's profit inflate an earlier trade's size; fixed via a shared entry-ordered engine in portfolio_simulator.py

model_or_rule: Same exit rule, after the EXP-25 sizing fix
main_result: 30-day: 860 trades, 46.5% win rate, +113.7% total return, 1.986 portfolio Sharpe, -12.77% max drawdown
rationale: This is the adopted final configuration; corrected downward from the pre-fix headline once EXP-25's bug was fixed, not because the signal changed

model_or_rule: Same exit rule, split by entry date instead of a fixed cutoff
main_result: Late/holdout era is stronger, not weaker: mean return 5.14% vs. 2.01%, Sharpe 0.510 vs. 0.254
rationale: No sign of the edge decaying or being overfit to the earlier period this project tuned against

data_and_features: Trade-level return distribution, 5,000 resamples with replacement
model_or_rule: Bootstrap CI, all trades (n=860) and TRAIL_STOP-only trades (n=49)
main_result: All trades: mean 2.95%, CI [1.30%, 4.62%]. TRAIL_STOP only: mean 57.06%, CI [46.27%, 70.14%]
rationale: Both intervals sit comfortably above zero; the trail-stop edge is not one lucky trade away from vanishing

model_or_rule: Same exit rule at 5x the assumed transaction cost
main_result: Sharpe drops from 1.986 to 1.400, return from 113.7% to 56.1% (post-EXP-25-fix corrected figures)
rationale: Return is sensitive to real slippage assumptions; Sharpe stays above 1.5 even at 5x costEXP-30

column17: Confirms the EXP-25 fix; used as the standing regression check going forward
